title: basic-auth fail-closed backstop: only response filters (filter_*/redact_*) exempt a route; after-request MANAGE grants and permission cleanups do not
answers: Why did a write route with no before-request check pass the basic-auth fail-closed net?
Which after-request handlers are allowed to skip the before-request authorization check?
How do I add a new after-request handler to a basic-auth route without opening an authorization gap?
body:
Path: The fail-closed authorization net in the basic-auth app for routes that have no before-request validator: mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:_authorized_outside_before_request decides whether a given path and method is exempt. It checks AFTER_REQUEST_HANDLERS keyed by (path, method) and the parameterized WORKSPACE_PARAMETERIZED_AFTER_REQUEST_HANDLERS.
Rule: Only handlers in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:_SELF_AUTHORIZING_AFTER_REQUEST_HANDLERS count as authorizing a route on their own. That set holds response filters (filter_search_*, filter_list_*, redact_secrets_config_for_non_admins). Ownership grants (set_can_manage_*) and permission cleanups (for example _cleanup_workspace_permissions) run after an already-authorized write, so their presence must not exempt a route. A new after-request handler that does not filter the response needs a before-request validator for its route. The test test_every_ownership_grant_route_has_a_before_request_validator in tests/server/auth/test_authorization_coverage.py enforces this for every set_can_manage_* route.
Symptom: The CreateGatewaySecret route had a MANAGE ownership grant after the request and no before-request validator. The grant made the route look authorized, so the fail-closed net never flagged it, and any account could create gateway secrets (GHSA-4449-4cjp-ffp5).
Constraints: Applies to the basic-auth app. Routes matched earlier by _HANDLER_INTERNAL_AUTHZ_SUFFIXES or the public-route check return before this function is reached. Response filters remain exempt because they decide visibility of the returned data. Adding a route to the self-authorizing set is a security decision and should be reviewed as one.
applies: Authorization fallback for any basic-auth route lacking a before-request validator, and any change to after-request handler registration.
says: Non-admin accounts can create gateway secrets without having required permissions.
Unauthorized users are able to perform write actions on protected endpoints.
Restrict creation of gateway secrets strictly to authorized administrative users.
Ensure every resource modification request verifies user permissions before executing.
search: In the basic-auth authorization framework, mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:_authorized_outside_before_request enforces that only response-filtering after-request handlers in _SELF_AUTHORIZING_AFTER_REQUEST_HANDLERS exempt a route. Ownership grants like set_can_manage_* and permission cleanups do not exempt routes, requiring write endpoints such as gateway secret creation to define explicit before-request validators. Applies to route authorization fallbacks in the basic-auth application, with test_every_ownership_grant_route_has_a_before_request_validator verifying coverage across all ownership-granting routes.
